newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mixed, seen strong on gas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mixed, seen strong on gas.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended mixed but unchanged Thursday, maintaining gains made earlier in the week based on strength in natural gas markets, industry sources said.
"Electricity is seeing a little bit of strength from gas," one New York-based futures broker said.
Traders said they expected some continued strength in power futures ahead of the colder, higher demand winter season.

November California-Oregon Border (COB) futures ended up eight cents at $18.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trade in a range of $17.85-18.25, while December settled up 17 cents at $19.15 after trade as high as $19.25 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds were steady to up to 20 cents higher.

November Palo Verde (PV) closed down seven cents at the day's low of $17.40 after hitting a new contract high of $18.20, while December PV settled down five cents at $17.75 per MWh from trade in a range of $18.00-18.25.
Remaining PV deferreds settled from 20 cents lower to 20 cents higher.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 158 COB and 97 PV contracts traded Thursday.
